inputs_used: Live old page https://weddedwonderland.com/22-amazing-table-settings-for-every-wedding-theme (read via Firecrawl, 2026-11-20; structure only, no wording, images or claims reused)

payload.title: Wedding Table Settings for Every Theme, Piece by Piece
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their thirties, around a year out from a destination wedding abroad with a six-figure AUD budget, who has a theme in mind and now needs to know exactly what goes on each guest's place (and in what order) so they can brief a venue or stylist they will meet only by email and video call.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about the reception: one click to the Wedded Concierge page from the closing line.
payload.angle: Page-one results are galleries of pretty tables. This page shows how a place setting is built, piece by piece and course by course, then translates each theme into concrete choices for those same pieces (plate, cutlery finish, glass shape, napkin fold, stationery), and adds the step galleries never cover for a wedding abroad: asking the venue what tableware it holds and what must be hired in before you fall in love with a look.
must_include: SECTION 'The place setting, piece by piece': (a) charger and plates, how the stack builds and what is cleared when; (b) cutlery order by course, working from the outside in, forks left, knives and spoons right, dessert cutlery above the plate; (c) glassware, set above the knives in the order it is used (water, then wines, then sparkling); (d) napkin placement and fold options; (e) name card and printed menu placement. Written as confident living practice, no stated origins or history.

SECTION 'Table settings by theme': regrouped from the old post's sound themes into roughly 6 to 8 groups, each translated into the same pieces (plates, cutlery finish, glassware, napkin, stationery). Suggested groups: Classic and formal (old Elegant, Regal, Extravagant); Pared back (Minimalist, Monochrome, Neutral); Garden and romantic (Pastel, Vintage, Spring); Coastal (Beachy, Summer); Country estate (Rustic, Woodland, Autumn); Winter and candlelit (Winter, with a short nod to a festive-season date); Playful and retro (Fun, Sixties). Planner may merge or rename. No number in the title or headings.

SECTION 'Destination weddings': framed as questions to ask the venue, e.g. What tableware, glassware and linen do you hold, and for how many guests? Which pieces would need to be hired in? Can we see the actual pieces or photos of them laid? Who sets and clears the tables? Are there limits on open flame or on outside suppliers? No answers asserted for any venue.

SECTION 'Planning your table settings': the table mock-up (what to check at it: spacing per guest, how the setting looks with centrepieces in place, sightlines, stationery proofs) and when to decide each element relative to menu, guest count and stationery deadlines. Timing given as relative sequence, not invented lead times; any specific lead time is [[VERIFY]].

Prominent link to /style-advice/wedding-table-decor near the top (scope line: this page covers the setting at each place; that page covers centrepieces, linen, florals and candles) and again in the theme section.

FAQ (4 to 6 questions), e.g. which side does the bread plate go; how many glasses per guest; where does the dessert cutlery go; should the napkin go on the plate or to the left; do we need chargers; can a venue abroad supply everything.

Close with exactly one Wedded Advisor line drawn from brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30. Preferred: 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit' (ties to the venue tableware questions). Alternative: 'One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.'
Internal links: /wonderland-concierge (primary CTA); /wonderland-studio for seating and name cards (secondary, natural fit with place cards).
avoid: Prices of any kind (no hire costs, per-head figures or From AUD numbers)
Vendor or brand names, including Casa de Perrin from the old post
Statistics, survey figures or trend claims
Research talk ('we analysed', 'according to our research', 'search results show')
Stated origins or history of etiquette conventions; write them as current practice
Decor depth: centrepieces, linen, florals and candles beyond one-line mentions; send to /style-advice/wedding-table-decor
Any claim about what a specific venue supplies
Competitor wording, images or Instagram embeds
A number in the title or H2s
